title: A Busy Saturday
text: Last Saturday I woke up early because the sun was shining through my window. After a quick breakfast, I took the bus to the market near the river. It was crowded, but the fruit looked fresh and the prices were reasonable. I bought some apples, a loaf of bread and a bunch of flowers for my grandmother. In the afternoon we sat in her garden, drank tea and talked about her childhood. She told me that life was harder then, but people were more patient and shared what they had with their neighbours.

title: Cities and Green Space
text: As cities expand, the amount of green space available to each resident tends to shrink. Researchers argue that this trend has serious consequences for public health. Access to parks has been linked to lower levels of stress, more regular physical activity and a stronger sense of community. However, creating new parks in crowded neighbourhoods is expensive, and local authorities must allocate limited land between green space and affordable housing. Some planners therefore propose a compromise: rooftop gardens and tree-lined streets, which occupy little land but still make residential areas more pleasant and sustainable.

title: Memory and Sleep
text: A growing body of evidence suggests that sleep plays a pivotal role in the consolidation of memory. During deep sleep, the brain appears to rehearse recently acquired information, strengthening the neural connections that underpin it. Conversely, chronic sleep deprivation impairs attention and undermines the capacity to retain new material, a deficit that cannot be fully offset by caffeine or sheer determination. These findings have prompted some educators to question the prevalent assumption that late-night revision is an efficient strategy, and to advocate schedules that are less detrimental to students' cognitive wellbeing.
